Separate from August 2021 eastern imported cases. National total.
retracted_reason: DEFINITIVE misattribution: the source (OCHA West and Central Africa Weekly Regional Humanitarian Snapshot 4-10 Oct 2022, metadata 13; read 2026-10-02 via Wayback capture http://web.archive.org/web/20221012193219/https://reliefweb.int/report/burkina-faso/west-and-central-africa-weekly-regional-humanitarian-snapshot-4-october-10-october-2022) prints the 12,517 cases / 254 deaths paragraph under the CAMEROON heading: 'CAMEROON As of 4 October, Cholera disease killed 254 persons and affected another 12,517, according to the ministry of public health. The disease mostly affected the south-west region since the beginning of the outbreak in October 2021.' The BURKINA FASO section of the same snapshot concerns UNHAS food deliveries to Djibo and does not mention cholera. source: UNICEF Burkina Faso Humanitarian Situation Report 2025
processing_notes: UNICEF Burkina Faso SitRep (Jan-Apr 2025) references 'more than 550 infections and 24 deaths in the Central Sahel region' for 2025. CFR approx 4.4% (24/550). WHO AFRO Monthly Cholera Bulletins (Jan-June 2025) do NOT list Burkina Faso among affected countries. Discrepancy may reflect different reporting thresholds. Confidence reduced due to WHO-UNICEF discrepancy. Nord region most affected (11%).
retracted_reason: DEFINITIVE: (1) The cited source (metadata 12, UNICEF Burkina Faso Humanitarian Situation Report No. 1, 1 Jan-30 Apr 2025, 11-page PDF downloaded from the metadata URL and read in full 2026-10-02) contains no mention of cholera: its 'Epidemiological Situation' section covers meningitis, measles (1,732 cases), dengue, hepatitis E in Centre-Nord and polio only; the strings '550', '24 deaths' and 'Central Sahel' with cholera do not occur, and the '11%' in the old note is a nutrition coverage figure. (2) A primary WHO table contradicts the row: WER 101(38), 25 Sep 2026, Cholera Annual Report 2025, Table 5 lists Burkina Faso among African Region countries reporting ZERO cholera cases in 2025 (new row 30), and Burkina Faso is absent from Table 1 (22 African countries with cases). (3) Africa CDC Epidemic Intelligence Report (issue 2026-09-20) lists 24 AU Member States with cholera in 2025, Burkina Faso not among them. Superseded by row 30 (2025 Documented_Absence).
